---
title: "Chi-square tests"
---

Every pair of categorical questions was cross-tabulated and tested for
independence with a chi-square test (`scipy.stats.chi2_contingency`, Yates'
correction applied at 1 degree of freedom). This page shows the p-values as
a heatmap — darker means a stronger association.

```{python}
# | echo: false
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent))

_CHI2 = Path.cwd().parent.parent / "data" / "public" / "chi2" / "chi2_test.csv"
chi2 = pd.read_csv(_CHI2)
chi2["neg_log10_p"] = -np.log10(chi2["p_value"].clip(lower=1e-300))
```

## All pairs

```{python}
# | echo: false
def heatmap(df, title):
    return (
        alt.Chart(df)
        .mark_rect()
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("x:N", title=None),
            y=alt.Y("y:N", title=None),
            color=alt.Color(
                "neg_log10_p:Q",
                title="-log10(p)",
                scale=alt.Scale(scheme="blues"),
            ),
            tooltip=["x", "y", alt.Tooltip("p_value:Q", format=".2e"), "statistic:Q", "dof:Q"],
        )
        .properties(width="container", height=520, title=title)
    )


heatmap(chi2, "All question pairs")
```

## Significant pairs (p < 0.05)

```{python}
# | echo: false
heatmap(chi2[chi2["p_value"] < 0.05], "Pairs with p < 0.05")
```

The strongest associations are between the geographic questions (Q03/Q04
region and subregion), and among the four DE&I aspects within Q12 and
within Q17.

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
Computed on the individual-level data locally; only the test statistics
(p-value, chi-square, degrees of freedom) are published, not any table of
counts.
:::
